story_events.title: A family in Geneva
story_events.summary: Elizabeth joins the Frankenstein household; Victor grows up with family affection and Henry’s friendship. This example follows selected events in chronological order, not the novel’s nested narration. Source: Mary Shelley, 1831 edition, chapters 1–2. Player/NPC types are current modeling labels; profile status and goals are not historical fields.

story_events.title: Caroline’s final wish
story_events.summary: Caroline nurses Elizabeth through scarlet fever, contracts the illness, and dies. She hopes Victor and Elizabeth will marry. Victor’s departure for Ingolstadt is delayed by grief. Chapter 3.

story_events.title: Waldman opens a door
story_events.summary: At Ingolstadt, Waldman encourages Victor to study modern science. Victor becomes absorbed in the origins of life. Chapters 3–4.

story_events.title: Life, followed by abandonment
story_events.summary: Victor animates the being he has assembled and recoils from him. The creature enters the visible cast here. The lasting Creator connection is separate from the changing relationship of responsibility and hostility. Chapter 5.

story_events.title: Clerval’s care
story_events.summary: Henry arrives and nurses Victor through a prolonged illness. Victor conceals the experiment. Chapters 5–6.

story_events.title: Learning beside the cottage
story_events.summary: The hidden creature observes De Lacey, Felix and Agatha, secretly gathers fuel, and learns through Safie’s lessons. Their earlier exile and the merchant’s betrayal are recounted here as backstory, not newly occurring actions. Chapters 11–14.

story_events.title: The appeal and the rejection
story_events.summary: The creature speaks to blind De Lacey, who hears him sympathetically. Felix returns and strikes him; Safie and Agatha react in fear. The family leaves. The creature later burns the empty cottage. Chapters 15–16.

story_events.title: William murdered; Justine framed
story_events.summary: Near Geneva, the creature kills William after learning his family name, then plants the miniature on the sleeping Justine. Victor later suspects the creature. The events are confessed retrospectively in chapter 16; their consequences appear in chapter 7.

story_events.title: Justine’s conviction
story_events.summary: Elizabeth testifies to Justine’s character. A coerced confession and circumstantial evidence lead to Justine’s execution. Victor’s silence leaves him consumed by guilt. Chapter 8.

story_events.title: The glacier bargain
story_events.summary: On the glacier, the creature tells his story and asks for a companion. Victor agrees on condition that the pair leave human society. Load the saved view for this scene to see a temporary agreement replace abandonment on the same connection. Chapters 10 and 17.

story_events.title: A journey with a secret purpose
story_events.summary: Victor travels with Henry through Britain, then separates from him to work alone in the Orkneys. Henry does not know what Victor is making. Chapters 18–19.

story_events.title: The companion destroyed
story_events.summary: Victor destroys the unfinished companion before animating her. The watching creature confronts him and threatens his wedding night. No living second creature is added: this is an uncompleted creation, recorded in the event. Chapter 20.

story_events.title: Henry’s death in Ireland
story_events.summary: Henry is murdered by the creature. Victor is accused, collapses, and is later cleared. Alphonse comes to support him. Chapters 21–22.

story_events.title: Victor and Elizabeth marry
story_events.summary: Victor marries Elizabeth while misreading the threat as directed chiefly against himself. The Intended marriage connection becomes Spouse at this event. Chapter 22.

story_events.title: The wedding-night murder
story_events.summary: The creature kills Elizabeth while Victor searches for an attacker elsewhere. Victor sees the creature outside. The active spousal relationship ends here; its earlier states remain in History. Chapter 23.

story_events.title: Alphonse dies of grief
story_events.summary: The death of Elizabeth overwhelms Alphonse, who dies soon afterward. Victor’s surviving purpose turns toward revenge. Chapter 23.

story_events.title: The pursuit north
story_events.summary: Victor vows vengeance and pursues the creature across vast distances. The creature leaves signs and provisions that prolong the chase. Their changing connection becomes mutual pursuit; the Creator connection remains a separate historical fact. Chapter 24.

story_events.title: Walton rescues Victor
story_events.summary: Walton’s crew takes the exhausted Victor aboard. Victor recounts the history that makes up most of the novel. Margaret appears as the recipient of Walton’s letters, not as a passenger physically present on the ship. Letter 4 and chapter 24.

story_events.title: A retreat and a death
story_events.summary: Walton agrees to return south when the ice permits, despite Victor’s appeal to ambition. Victor dies aboard the ship. The pursuit ends; Walton’s choice interrupts the repetition of Victor’s obsession. Walton’s continuation, chapter 24.

story_events.title: The creature’s farewell
story_events.summary: The creature mourns over Victor’s body, speaks with Walton about guilt and suffering, and announces that he will destroy himself. He departs on an ice raft. The novel does not show his death. Walton’s continuation, chapter 24. Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/42324/42324-h/42324-h.htm
